text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - Leading shares finished higher for the fifth day running, but trading volumes remained thin as many investor opted to stay on sidelines due to continued political and economic uncertainties. The FTSE 100 index, which had risen 58.8 points the previous four sessions, ended 18.2 points higher to 4,328.7.

FRANKFURT - The share market ended the day nearly one percentage point lower, as worries about U.S. rate rises and the fate of Europe's monetary union added to price volatility. The IBIS DAX index of electronic trade in 30 German blue-chip stocks ended the day down 32.79 points, or 0.98 percent, at 3,328.41 points. Earlier, the 30-share DAX, having hit a low of 3,306.15 points in the pre-bourse IBIS electronic phase, closed the bourse session up 3.19 points, or 0.10 percent at 3,347.58.

PARIS - Shares finished with a big loss as political risk stalked the markets. Traders said the market was waiting for confirmation that President Jacques Chirac would dissolve parliament and set a parliamentary election date, either in late May or early June. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 24.89 points or 0.98 percent at 2,522.67.

ZURICH - Shares closed with a record high in a session that also saw a new all-time high of 4,756.3 points on the blue-chip SMI index. The market was characterised by selective buying adding the positive development of some shares supported the market. The blue-chip SMI rose 41 points or 0.87 percent to 4,740.1 points. The broad SPI added 21.8 points or 0.71 percent at 2,990.30 points.

TOKYO - Stocks ended sharply higher with the Nikkei benchmark average closing above 18,500 for the first time in a month, buoyed by buying of chemical and steel stocks. Brokers said buy-backs of financial sector issues also lifted the market. The 225-share Nikkei average finished 199.52 points or 1.09 percent higher at 18,551.66.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed higher, due chiefly to positive local sentiment in the longer term outlook for the major property developers. The Hang Seng Index gained 84.86 points to close at 12,626.04 after hitting a high for the day of 12,711.31 on a surprisingly strong rebound in the morning session.

SYDNEY - The share market closed slightly firmer with the continuing rally on the Wall Street market underpinning the optimistic sentiment for local traders. The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index ended 3.4 points up at 2,445.8, after touching an intra-day high of 2,454.5.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended trade steadier with industrials softening after early gains on the back of Friday's stronger Wall Street and golds heeding bullion's slight recoveries. Dealers said the market's sentiment was cautious to bullish, but market players awaited cues from some of this week's economic indicators due for release. The industrial index closed 22.5 points up at 8,338, the all-share ended up 17.8 points to 7,040 and the gold index gained 9.9 points to finish at 1,257.6.
